pn: Lakkhaṇa 01. Son of Dasaratha and brother of Rāma, Sītā and Bharata. He is identified with Sāriputta. Ja.iv.130; for details see the Dasarathajātaka (Ja 461).
Lakkhaṇa 02. One of the eight Brahmins who recognized the auspicious signs at the birth of the Bodhisatta (Ja.i.56). The Milinda (Mil. 236) speaks of him as one of the Buddha’s first teachers.

Lakkhaṇa 03. Lakkhaṇa Thera. Mentioned as having stayed with Mahā Moggallāna on Gijjhakūṭa. Once, when they were going down to Rājagaha for alms, Lakkhaṇa noticed that at a certain spot Moggallāna smiled; on asking him why, he was told to wait till they saw the Buddha. When the question was repeated in the Buddha’s presence, Moggallāna said that he had smiled on seeing various Petas with gruesome forms flying through the air. From the text it would appear that these visions were seen again on several occasions. SN.ii.254; Vin.iii.104ff.; the stories of some of the Petas seen and of their past lives are given in detail in Dhp-a.ii.68ff.; iii.60ff.; 410ff., 479.

The Commentary (SN-a.ii.159) explains that Lakkhaṇa was one of the thousand Jaṭilas ordained by the Buddha (when he converted the Tebhātikajaṭilas). He attained Arahant-ship at the conclusion of the preaching of the Ādittapariyāya desanā. He was called Lakkhaṇa because of his marvellous personality, “like unto Brahma’s” (Brahmasamena). It adds further that Lakkhaṇa’s failure to see the Petas was not because he lacked the divine eye but because he was not giving attention (anāvajjento), as a clairvoyant must. It is said (Vin.iii.105) that when Moggallāna related his vision, some of the monks blamed him for claiming superhuman powers (uttarimanussadhamma), but the Buddha declared him free from blame.
Lakkhaṇa 04. A deer, son of the Bodhisatta, identified with Sāriputta. For his story see the Lakkhaṇajātaka.

Lakkhana：1．Lakkhana． Son of Dasaratha and brother of Rāma，Sītā and Bharata．He is identified with Sāriputta．J．iv．130； for details see the Dasaratha Jātaka．

2．Lakkhana．One of the eight brahmins who recognized the auspicious signs at the birth of the Buddha （J．i．56）．The Milinda （Mil．236） speaks of him as one of the Buddha’s first teachers．

3．Lakkhana Thera．Mentioned as having stayed with Mahā Moggallāna on Gijjhakūta．Once，when they were going down to Rājagaha for alms，Lakkhana noticed that at a certain spot Moggallāna smiled； on asking him why，he was told to wait till they saw the Buddha．When the question was repeated in the Buddha’s presence，Moggallāna said that he had smiled on seeing various Petas with gruesome forms flying through the air．From the text it would appear that these visions were seen again on several occasions．S．ii．254； Vin．iii．104ff．； the stories of some of the Petas seen and of their past lives are given in detail in DhA．ii．68ff．； iii．60ff．； 410ff．，479．

The Commentary （SA．ii．159） explains that Lakkhana was one of the thousand Jatilas ordained by the Buddha （when he converted the Tebhātika Jatilas）．He attained arahantship at the conclusion of the preaching of the ādittapariyāyadesanā．He was called Lakkhana because of his marvellous personality，”like unto Brahmā’s” （brahmasamena）．It adds further that Lakkhana’s failure to see the Petas was not because he lacked the divine eye but because he was not giving attention （anāvajjento），as a clairvoyant must．It is said （Vin．iii．105） that when Moggallāna related his vision，some of the monks blamed him for claiming superhuman powers （uttarimanussadhamma），but the Buddha declared him free from blame．

4．Lakkhana．A deer，son of the Bodhisatta，identified with Sāriputta．For his story see the Lakkhana Jātaka．

lakkhaṇasutta.p: [Lakkhaṇa+sutta] (na) CL=8 Lakkhaṇa Sutta( sutta which is preaching about  showing The thirty two distinctive features or signs on the persons of the Buddhas).
pn: Lakkhaṇasutta. The thirtieth Sutta of the Dīghanikāya. It gives an account of the thirty-two special marks of the superman (mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni) which signify that their possessor will be either a world emperor (Cakkavatti) or a Buddha. The Sutta definitely states that these marks are entirely due to good deeds done in former births and can only be maintained in the present life by goodness. DN.iii.142-79; the Sutta is quoted in Mil. p. 405.

lakuṇḍaka.p: [Lakuḍi+a+ka] (ti) CL=8 Laku+ḍi+a+ka. Lakuḍivāmanatthe,a, sakatthe ko, lakuviya ghaṭikāviya ḍeti pavattetīti vā lakuṇḍako, dhāna, ṭī. 319.]  (1) who is short (heigh) (or) squat. Lakuṇḍakasarīra, lakuṇḍakapāda - See them. (2) Lakuṇḍaka Suttam (3) who is squat, who is short height. (4) (A)  the young man called Lakuṇḍaka bhaddiya, (B) Lakuṇḍaka bhaddiya Thera.
a: လကု+ဍိ+အ+က။ လကုဍိဝါမနတ္ထေ၊အ၊ သကတ္ထေ ကော၊ လကုဝိယ ဃဋိကာဝိယ ဍေတိ ပဝတ္တေတီတိ ဝါ လကုဏ္ဍကော၊ ဓာန်၊ ဋီ။ ၃၁၉။] (၁)ပုကွ-တို-နည်း-သော။ လကုဏ္ဍကသရီရ, လကုဏ္ဍကပါဒ-တို့ကြည့်။(၂)လကုဏ္ဍကသုတ်။(၃)ပုကွသူ၊ အရပ်ပုသူ။(၎)(က)လကုဏ္ဍကဘဒ္ဒိယ-လုလင်-အမျိုးသား(ခ)လကုဏ္ဍကဘဒ္ဒိယထေရ်။

B:
lakuṇḍaka： lakuṇḍaka（ti）
လကုဏ္ဍက（တိ）
[akuḍi+a+ka．laku+ḍi+a+ka．lakuḍivāmanatthe，a，sakatthe ko，lakuviya ghaṭikāviya ḍeti pavattetīti vā lakuṇḍako，，ṭī．319．]
[လကုဍိ+အ+က။ လကု+ဍိ+အ+က။ လကုဍိဝါမနတေ္ထ၊အ၊ သကတေ္ထ ကော၊ လကုဝိယ ဃဋိကာဝိယ ဍေတိ ပဝတေ္တတီတိ ဝါ လကုဏ္ဍကော၊ ဓာန်၊ ဋီ။ ၃၁၉။]
K:
lakuṇḍaka：လကုဏ္ဍက（တိ）
[လကုဍိ+အ+က။ လကု+ဍိ+အ+က။ လကုဍိဝါမနတေ္ထ၊အ၊ သကတေ္ထ ကော၊ လကုဝိယ ဃဋိကာဝိယ ဍေတိ ပဝတေ္တတီတိ ဝါ လကုဏ္ဍကော၊ ဓာန်၊ ဋီ။ ၃၁၉။]
（၁） ပုကွ-တို-နည်း-သော။ လကုဏ္ဍကသရီရ，လကုဏ္ဍကပါဒ-တို့ကြည့်။ （၂） လကုဏ္ဍကသုတ်။ （၃） ပုကွသူ၊ အရပ်ပုသူ။ （၄） （က） လကုဏ္ဍကဘဒ္ဒိယ-လုလင်-အမျိုးသား （ခ） လကုဏ္ဍကဘဒ္ဒိယထေရ်။

lakuṇḍakabhaddiya.p: [Lakuṇḍaka+bhaddiya] (pu) CL=8 Lakuṇḍaka bhaddiya young man (or) Lakuṇḍaka bhaddiya Thera, Lakuṇḍaka bhaddiya Thera. Lakuṇḍaka-(4-ka, kha) - See.
a: လကုဏ္ဍကဘဒ္ဒိယ(ပု)
[လကုဏ္ဍက+ဘဒ္ဒိယ]
လကုဏ္ဍကဘဒ္ဒိယ-လုလင်-အမျိုးသား-ထေရ်၊ လကုဏ္ဍကဘဒ္ဒိယထေရ်။ လကုဏ္ဍက-(၎-က, ခ)-ကြည့်။

lākhātamba.p: [Lākhā+tamba] (ti) CL=8 It has red hairs, as if it had been dyed with wax liquid.
